source_boundary_rules: If the uploaded book directly says it, place it in directly_supported_claims.
If the book implies it through method structure or examples, place it in inferred_claims.

confidence_calibration.high: Direct definitions, method descriptions, theorem meanings, proof summaries, or source-supported error-estimation concepts.
confidence_calibration.medium: Cross-section synthesis or applied ML guidance strongly grounded in the book but dependent on context.
confidence_calibration.low: Software-current behavior, vendor/export schemas, restaurant analytics overlay, OMAKAI-style applications, AI-agent deployment assumptions, or claims requiring real data validation.

model_selection_checklist: Define whether the task is classification, regression, clustering, dimensionality reduction, anomaly detection, forecasting, reporting, or causal inference.
Specify X, Y, prediction time, loss/metric, sample mechanism, and intended action before choosing an algorithm.
Compare a simple baseline before complex models.

Match method assumptions to data: covariance structure for LDA/QDA, metric for nearest-neighbor/kernel methods, capacity/regularization for SVM/NN/tree methods, cluster shape for K-means/GMM, stationarity/time structure for forecasting.
When feature/model/threshold choices are tuned, separate selection from final performance assessment with nested validation or an untouched test set.
Check sample size against dimensionality and model complexity; prefer simpler models when the complexity-to-sample-size ratio is poor.
validation_leakage_checklist: Was every feature available before the prediction decision?
Was preprocessing fit only on training folds in each validation split?
Was feature selection nested inside validation?
Was PCA/dimensionality reduction fit only on training data/folds?
Were repeated customers, locations, weeks, menu items, or duplicated records kept from leaking across train/test boundaries?
Is the validation split time-aware for future predictions?
Does the final evaluation reflect deployment distribution, not only a convenient historical slice?
Are target leakage, proxy leakage, and post-outcome notes removed?
Is the test set independent and representative enough for the claim being made?
error_estimation_rules: Training or apparent error measures fit to the same data used for design; it is not future generalization evidence.
Independent test-set error is conceptually clean but requires held-out labeled data large and representative enough for the intended claim.
Cross-validation estimates the full training procedure only if all preprocessing, selection, thresholding, and tuning are inside each fold.
Bootstrap can help in small samples but must respect unit dependence and the full design procedure.
Bolstered error estimation is source-supported but should not be substituted mechanically for a representative deployment evaluation.
Model selection by validation error creates selection bias unless a separate final evaluation or nested design is used.
High-dimensional small-sample settings require special caution because feature selection, covariance estimation, and flexible classifiers can be unstable.
restaurant_analytics_decision_gate: What decision are we trying to improve?
Is this prediction, classification, clustering, anomaly detection, forecasting, reporting, or causal inference?
What data exists before the decision?
Are locations comparable or should they be modeled separately?
What seasonality, holiday, event, promo, menu, weather, or operational confounders exist?
What validation design proves this works?
What operational action would change if the model is right?
What is the simplest useful non-ML baseline?
What would make this conclusion unsafe?
omakai_safe_use_warnings: Restaurant analytics content is an operational overlay, not direct book content.
Do not invent OMAKAI facts, current export schemas, or current platform behavior.
Prediction is not causation; promo, marketing, staffing, or menu conclusions need causal design or careful quasi-experimental evidence.
Reviews and delivery-platform ratings may be nonrandom samples; do not treat them as all-guest satisfaction without evidence.
Location comparisons require controls for location mix, daypart, calendar, seasonality, holiday, event, promo, menu, weather, and operational changes.
A model that predicts a risk is useful only if a feasible action, owner, threshold, and monitoring plan exist.
ai_agent_response_standard: State task type, target, evidence reviewed, and source-vs-extension boundary.
Name the relevant record IDs and risk IDs.
Separate direct source claims from inferred claims and operational guidance.
Ask for missing evidence instead of filling gaps with assumptions.
For software-current or vendor-export claims, mark current verification required unless official docs/current runtime/current export sample were checked.
For restaurant analytics, define what the model output would mean and would not mean before recommending action.
current_verification_rules: Do not silently modernize Python, scikit-learn, Jupyter, NumPy, SciPy, deep-learning frameworks, datasets, or vendor export behavior.
Use official documentation, current runtime output, or current export samples for software/API/schema claims.
Current-verification flags must point to valid record IDs; every V1.1 flag does so.
If only the book is available, discuss the method conceptually and mark implementation details as unverified.

Bayes classifier: Minimum-error benchmark using posterior probabilities.
Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA): Linear Gaussian discriminant classifier with shared covariance.
Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA): Quadratic Gaussian discriminant classifier with class-specific covariance.
Logistic classifier: Probability-style classifier using a logistic link.
Nearest-neighbor classifier: Classifies by nearby labeled points.
Kernel classifier: Smooths local class information using a kernel and bandwidth.
Support Vector Machine (SVM): Margin classifier, optionally nonlinear via kernels.
Neural-network classifier: Flexible layer-based function approximation for labels.
Decision tree: Recursive feature-space partition into decision leaves.
Cross-validation: Rotates held-out folds to estimate a learning procedure.
Bootstrap: Uses resampling with replacement for error/variability estimation.
Bolstered error estimation: Smooths around sample points to estimate classification error.
Feature selection: Selects useful variables or terms.
Principal Component Analysis (PCA): Unsupervised variance-based feature transformation.
K-means: Partitions unlabeled data by distances to K centers.
Gaussian mixture model (GMM): Probabilistic Gaussian mixture clustering.
Expectation-Maximization (EM): Iterative latent-variable likelihood optimization.
Linear regression: Fits linear numeric prediction, commonly least squares.
Penalized regression: Ridge/LASSO/elastic-net shrink or select coefficients.
Gaussian process regression: Kernel-based probabilistic regression with predictive uncertainty.
Physics-informed neural network (PINN): Neural net constrained by PDE/data/boundary losses.
Physics-informed Gaussian process: Gaussian process constrained by differential operators or physics priors.

Training error mistaken for generalization: Training-set fit is treated as future performance.
Validation or test leakage: Held-out information affects preprocessing, tuning, labels, thresholds, or model choice.
Feature-selection leakage: Variables are selected using all labels before error estimation.
PCA-before-split leakage: Dimensionality reduction or scaling is fit using validation/test rows.
Model-selection bias: The winning validation score is optimistic after repeated search.
Small-sample instability: A small sample relative to model complexity makes boundaries and scores unstable.
High-dimensional overfitting: Many features with limited samples encourage noise-fitting and peaking behavior.
Class-prior shift: Class proportions differ between training/evaluation and deployment.
Bayes error overclaim: An empirical score is described as the Bayes error.
Bayes classifier unavailable: The Bayes rule is claimed without known posteriors or distributional assumptions.
LDA covariance mismatch: LDA is used despite implausible shared covariance or unstable pooled covariance.
QDA underpowered: Separate covariance matrices are estimated with too few cases or too many features.
Distance metric mismatch: Neighbor, kernel, clustering, or MDS results depend on unjustified distances or scaling.
Kernel bandwidth misuse: Bandwidth is chosen or interpreted without validation or sensitivity review.
Neural-network superiority assumption: A flexible neural network is assumed better without baseline and validation evidence.
Cluster reification: Algorithmic clusters are treated as real segments, causes, or stable categories.
Regression extrapolation: Numeric predictions are trusted outside observed feature/time support.
Physics model invalid: A physics-informed method is used with an invalid or irrelevant governing model.
Hard constraint invalid: An exact constraint encodes a false assumption into the model.
Software default drift: Python, scikit-learn, Jupyter, NumPy/SciPy, or ML-library behavior is assumed current.
Nonrandom review sample: Observed reviews are treated as representative of all guests.
Platform selection bias: A platform-specific stream is generalized to all channels or guest experiences.
Location confounding: Location differences masquerade as model drivers or operational effects.
Seasonality/event confounding: Holiday, event, weekday, promo, weather, or menu effects are mistaken for model signal.
Operational actionability gap: A prediction is produced without a decision owner, threshold, or action.
Correlation treated as causation: Predictive association is reported as causal effect.
Temporal split mismatch: Random splits are used for future forecasting or behavior prediction.
Duplicate entity leakage: The same customer, order, location, or week leaks across train/test rows.
Noisy or ambiguous labels: Ratings, complaints, or human themes are treated as flawless ground truth.
Define target before model: Ask for Y, feature timing, loss, and action before recommending algorithms.
Classification/regression gate: Use labels for classification, numeric targets for regression, and no target for clustering.
Clustering is not prediction: Treat clusters as hypotheses unless labels and prediction loss are defined.
Simple baseline first: Require majority-class, naive forecast, simple rule, or linear baseline before complexity.
Holdout before claim: Use independent validation/test evidence for future performance claims.
Feature selection inside split: Run feature selection within each training fold or inner loop.
PCA inside pipeline: Fit PCA/scaling/learned transforms only on training data for each split.
Nested validation for search: Use nested validation or final untouched test after extensive search.
Time-aware forecast validation: Use chronological/blocked validation for future sales or repeat behavior.
LDA/QDA covariance gate: Prefer LDA when shared covariance is plausible or samples are small; use QDA only with stable class covariance estimates.
Distance method scaling: Justify metric and scaling before nearest-neighbor, kernel, K-means, or MDS interpretation.
Neural net not default: Require data volume, baseline gain, and validation discipline before neural networks.
Regression extrapolation warning: Flag predictions outside historical support or ordinary operating regime.
PINNs only with physics: Use physics-informed methods only when a valid scientific constraint is central.
Hard-constraint check: Use hard constraints only when the constraint is correct for deployment.
Current documentation verification: Verify current Python/scikit-learn/NumPy/SciPy/Jupyter/export behavior before asserting it.
OMAKAI-safe restaurant ML gate: Run the 12-question restaurant decision gate before ML on restaurant data.
Review sample boundary: Limit review analytics to the observed review channel unless representativeness is proven.
Location blocking: Use location-aware validation or separate location models when location effects matter.
Seasonality/promo/event control: Annotate and separate calendar, event, promo, menu, weather, and operational confounders.
Prediction-to-action gate: Require action owner, threshold, timing, and human review before deployment.
Causal claim blocker: Use association/prediction wording unless a causal design supports intervention claims.
Dashboard warning layer: Show sample, leakage, confidence, validation, and action caveats beside scores.
When not to use ML: Prefer reporting, QA, thresholds, or experiments when no validated predictive action exists.

Model evaluation audit: Classify the score and detect leakage/model-selection bias.

Restaurant ML problem framing: Run the OMAKAI-safe decision gate before restaurant modeling.
Guest satisfaction classification review: Audit satisfaction target, sample representativeness, leakage, validation, and action.
Review text clustering/classification review: Choose classification if labels exist; clustering if discovering themes.
Sales forecasting review: Validate forecasts with time-aware splits and baseline comparisons.
Marketing attribution warning review: Block causal overclaim in marketing and promo analysis.
Location-level validation review: Match location claims to grouped or location-aware validation.
Leakage audit for restaurant datasets: Draw feature/target windows and remove future or duplicate entity leakage.
Prediction-to-action review: Require owner, threshold, timing, and human review before action.
Simple baseline-first review: Use a non-ML or simple ML baseline as minimum evidence.
Decide when not to use ML: Reject ML when reporting/QA/rules/causal design is the real need.
Classifier/regressor/clusterer selection review: Shortlist algorithms by target, assumptions, n/p, split, and risks.
AI-agent code review for scikit-learn-style pipelines: Inspect code for split, pipeline, leakage, and current API assumptions.
Owner dashboard warning review: Ensure dashboards expose validation, sample bias, caveats, and action triggers.
Restaurant export/schema verification review: Verify current R365/SevenRooms/Uber Eats/Sheets/Excel schemas from current samples.
